Documentation → Administration → Deploy clone

Deploy clone — copy one SATOM installation into another

Copy a SATOM deploy's configuration — appliances, credentials, users, settings, scripts, schedules — into a different installation, without backups or history, without either node's encryption key ever leaving it, and with the copy held until you release it.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → Source of Truth & Backup → Deploy Clone (URL /settings/#tab-deployclone), or the server shell on the primary — satom execute clone export | import | release, satom get clone status

What is it?#

A deploy clone copies the configuration of one SATOM installation into another one — a lab into production, an old pair into a new pair. It is not a restore: a system backup bundle puts the same deploy back the way it was and carries that deploy's ciphertext. A clone moves configuration between two installations that each keep their own FERNET_KEY, their own identity and their own HA pair.

What does it do?#

  • Exports the configuration only into one .tar.gz: appliances and their credentials, users, profiles and settings, scheduled action definitions, templates, exceptions, probes, dashboards, the wiki and the API library, Script Library scripts and schedules, integration hooks, WAF artifacts and branding.
  • Leaves behind everything that is not configuration: backups (the device vault and the system bundles), config history (the SoT store and the live config tree), the device cache, runs, logs, samples, incidents, notifications and firmware images. The first device sync after the release reads the device cache again from the appliances.
  • Never moves a key. Every encrypted value — credential columns, settings, and encrypted values inside JSON settings — is re-encrypted under a one-time transfer key. That key is sealed with a passphrase (scrypt + AES-GCM) that the export shows once and stores nowhere. The import re-encrypts every value under the target's own key.
  • Keeps the target's identity: HA role and peer, node certificate and identity key, backup server, signature store, recovery escrow and alert state are the target's before and after.
  • Holds the copy. After an import every scheduled action, Script Library schedule and hook that was enabled is switched off, and so are alert e-mail and the NetBox push, until you run clone release.
  1. 1Source: Export → download (or copy) the bundle → Target: Upload → Import → check → Release

Requirements#

  • An administrator account on both deploys (web console), or root on the server shell. Export, import and release run on the primary; on a standby the pane is read-only and the CLI refuses.
  • Both deploys on the same SATOM version. The import compares the database schema revision and every table's columns and refuses on any difference.
  • The passphrase the export showed.

Permissions#

  • Web console: the Deploy Clone pane needs Manage users (users.manage), like the rest of the admin console.
  • Server shell: the clone verbs require root (sudo satom …). satom get clone status works for any user.

How to use#

From the web console#

Open Settings → Source of Truth & Backup → Deploy Clone. It is not Clone / Migrate under Fleet & Devices, which copies configuration between appliances (Clone / Migrate settings).

  1. Export (on the source): click Export. The passphrase appears in the page straight away. Write it down: it is shown once and cannot be recovered. When the job ends, the bundle is listed under the button. Download it.
  2. Upload (on the target): choose the file and click Upload. The page shows where the bundle comes from, its tables, rows and files, and every reason it cannot be imported here.
  3. Import: enter the passphrase, type IMPORT and click Replace this deploy's configuration. The passphrase is checked before anything is queued. Your session ends with everyone else's: log in again with the source's account. Recent clone jobs shows each step.
  4. Check the appliances and schedules, and make sure the source no longer acts on the same appliances.
  5. Release: the Held after an import card lists what is held. Type RELEASE and click Release.

Export and import run in the privileged runner, not in the web process: an import has to stop the web service that serves the page. The passphrase reaches the runner in the request file only. The runner deletes that file before it does anything else, and the passphrase is never written to a job's status.

From the server shell#

  1. Export on the source primary: sudo satom execute clone export shows what the bundle carries; add --yes to write it. The bundle lands in data/clone-exports/. Write down the passphrase — it is shown once.
  2. Copy the file to the target primary (for example with scp).
  3. Preview on the target: sudo satom execute clone import <file> shows where the bundle comes from, how many tables, rows and files it holds, and every step the import will take. Nothing changes.
  4. Import: sudo satom execute clone import <file> --yes. The passphrase is asked on the terminal (or read from SATOM_CLONE_PASSPHRASE); it is never taken from the command line.
  5. Check the appliances and schedules on the target, and make sure the source no longer acts on the same appliances.
  6. Release: sudo satom execute clone release lists what is held; --yes switches it back on.

satom get clone status (any user) shows the last import and whether the node is still holding it.

Result#

  • The target serves the source's appliances, credentials, settings, scripts and users. You log in with the source's accounts, and every browser session opened on the target before the import is logged out.
  • The target's own history, device cache and backup index are emptied: those rows name appliances by number, and the numbers now belong to the source's appliances. Its system bundles, firmware and signature store are kept.
  • The replaced file sets of the target, and its device vault, live config tree and SoT store, are kept under data/clone-prev-<time>/.
  • Until the first device sync after the release, the appliances show no objects.
  • A safety bundle of the target's previous database is in the System Backup list; satom execute restore db <bundle> --yes puts it back.
  • clone release re-enables exactly what the import held — what was already off on the source stays off — and computes each schedule's next run from now, so the held period is not replayed.

Troubleshooting#

"could not open the transfer key: wrong passphrase, or the bundle has been altered"#

Possible causes - The passphrase was mistyped, or belongs to another export. - The bundle was modified after the export.

Solution 1. Retype the passphrase printed by that export. 2. If it still fails, export again on the source and copy the new file.

Verification - The import gets past the passphrase step. Nothing on the target changed while it failed.

"schema revision differs: bundle …, this node …"#

Possible causes - The two deploys run different SATOM versions.

Solution 1. Update the older deploy (see Software update) so both run the same version. 2. Export again from the source, then import.

Verification - satom get system status shows the same version on both.

"this bundle was exported from this deploy (same FERNET_KEY)"#

Possible causes - The bundle is being imported on the deploy that exported it.

Solution 1. To put this deploy back to an earlier state, use a database bundle: satom execute restore db <bundle> --yes (see System backup).

Verification - The restore reports pg_restore rc=0.

"table … is missing or altered" / "file set … is missing or altered"#

Possible causes - The copy of the bundle is truncated or was modified.

Solution 1. Copy the file again and compare its size with the source's.

Verification - The import preview runs without listing problems.

"The file is larger than this page accepts"#

Possible causes - The bundle is bigger than the upload limit of the front end (400 MB on a standard install).

Solution 1. Copy the file to the target primary (for example with scp) and import it from the server shell: sudo satom execute clone import <file> --yes.

Verification - The import's steps appear in Recent clone jobs, or the CLI prints them.

"table … is not configuration and must not travel" / "not a SATOM clone bundle (format 'satom-clone/1')"#

Possible causes - The bundle was written by an earlier build that also carried backups and history (format satom-clone/1), or it was edited to carry a table the target leaves behind.

Solution 1. Update the source to the same SATOM version as the target and export again.

Verification - The upload preview (or sudo satom execute clone import <file>) lists no problems.

"a clone export is already queued" / "… is already running"#

Possible causes - A clone job started a moment ago (or from another browser) has not finished.

Solution 1. Wait for it: Recent clone jobs shows its state. 2. If it stays at queued, the privileged runner is not picking requests up: satom get system health on the node shows its updater line, and sudo satom execute enable updater switches satom-updater.path back on.

Verification - The job reaches success or failed, and a new one can be queued.

After clicking Import, the page says the session ended#

Possible causes - This is expected. The import replaces the accounts with the source's and ends every session opened before it.

Solution 1. Log in with the source deploy's username and password. 2. Open Deploy Clone again: Recent clone jobs shows whether the import succeeded, and the Held after an import card appears.

Verification - Recent clone jobs shows the import as success.

The import lists "secrets this node cannot open"#

Possible causes - The source already held values its own key could not open (the export warns about these as token-shaped values copied as they are).

Solution 1. Re-enter the affected credentials on the target (for an appliance: edit it and save the password again).

Verification - satom diagnose recovery and a device sync of the affected appliance succeed.

Advanced#

  • External vault. A credential kept in the external vault travels as its vault marker. The target reaches it through the same vault configuration, which travels with the bundle; the export says how many such credentials there are.
  • What stays behind on purpose: queued Script Library and hook requests (the target would run them a second time), the node's leases, and its signature store, which every node fetches for itself.
  • Partial clones (by category or by appliance, merged into a deploy that keeps its own data) are not available yet.
